target_customer: Blockchain projects and ICO issuers that pay for smart contract security audits
problem: Smart contract bugs and hacks such as the DAO hack cost investors money. Quantstamp audits contracts and aimed to automate verification.
business_model: Fee-based security audits and assessments, later monitoring and advisory services; original plan to use the QSP token

founders.name: Richard Ma
founders.background_notes: YC page and company page call him founder and CEO. Secondary low quality sources mention a co-founder and CTO whose surname is spelled Stewart or Stuart, but no source opened confirms it, so no second founder is listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Formal verification and automated analysis of smart contracts were research-heavy in 2017, though most revenue came from manual audits.

defensibility.rationale: Audit track record and client trust build reputation, but the audit service is staffed expertise rather than a technical lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition occurred. Quantstamp remained independent and grew to 1,400 plus audits per its site; a 2023 SEC order settled the unregistered 2017 token offering.

market_need_then: The 2017 ICO boom and the DAO hack created strong demand for audits; Quantstamp raised over 28 million dollars in a token sale and claimed 484 audits by June 2018 (CoinDesk).

identity.logo: Simple logo intended to work on any medium per an unverified Steemit summary of a Ma interview
identity.visual_style: Security and trust oriented web3 branding
identity.voice_and_tone: Professional security voice with a monthly hack roundup blog

branding.brand_signature: Trust stamp positioning (VeriSign of blockchain analogy in a Hackernoon article) and audit badge on client projects
branding.community_and_virality: QSP token holders formed a community and criticized the team in 2018 (CoinDesk) over accepting dollars and ether instead of QSP; the company ran a community rewards system that it later ended.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong audit client list and recognition in web3 security, though the 2018 token controversy and the 2023 SEC settlement dented trust.

pivots.from: Automated decentralized smart contract auditing protocol paid in QSP
pivots.to: Manual and hybrid audits paid in dollars and ether, later broad web3 security services
pivots.why: CoinDesk June 2018 reports the company accepted dollars and ether out of necessity because the protocol was still under development; the SEC order says the platform was completed in June 2019 and later no longer supported.

outcome_analysis: Quantstamp rode the 2017 ICO wave with a 28 million dollar token sale and became a leading web3 security auditor with over a thousand audits and about 80 staff. It shifted from an automated token-based protocol to conventional audit services, and in 2023 settled SEC charges over the unregistered token sale with about 3.5 million dollars in total payments. It remains active.
notes: Competitors: no source dated near the batch naming rivals was found (CoinDesk 2018 and Medium analyses name none in the results), so the list is left empty. The round is the QSP token sale in Oct and Nov 2017 per the SEC order, which predates the batch; it was a token offering, not equity. Aggregators list a seed of 120 thousand dollars (2018) and about 3 million dollars (March 2019, Vitalik Buterin as angel) and a 2023 Series A II; all unverified single-aggregator figures. SEC penalty: 1,979,201 disgorgement, 494,314 interest, 1,000,000 penalty, one outlet cites 3.5 million total. A securities class action is also reported. Ma's education and employers were only on low quality sites and are left null.
